newsitem.title: USA: Rexrodt says no G7 text yet on greenhouse gases.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt says no G7 text yet on greenhouse gases.

text.p: German economics minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Friday evening that the Group of Seven industrialized nations had not yet agreed a formulation on greenhouse gas emissions for its Denver communique.
"The G7 are not yet in agreement about goals or about what the formulation should be in the final communique," he told reporters following a meeting with financial officials from other G7 nations.
Rexrodt said there were two draft formulations under consideration for the final text.

Under the first version, the G7 would call for the emission of greenhouse gases to be significantly below 1990 levels by 2005. But a second version, preferred by the European Union G7 members, would call for a 15 percent reduction by 2010 compared with 1990, he added.

Rexrodt said it was not clear whether the issue would be resolved by the government aides or sherpas overnight, or whether the government leaders would have to take the decision on the final formulation.
"But I am optimistic that a solution will be found," he said.
The Group of Seven comprises Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States.
